prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological phase of time-reversal-invariant insulators, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B042 as my preferred single-achievement prize, and after the first round I can state more precisely why. The physics distinction the chair asks for is this. The Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz lineage of 2016 rests on a Chern number, a topological invariant of a band structure with broken time-reversal symmetry, which gives a quantized Hall conductance. Kane and Mele showed that with time-reversal symmetry intact, spin-orbit coupling produces a different, Z2-valued invariant, protected by Kramers degeneracy, with no net Hall conductance but with a pair of counter-propagating helical edge modes. That is a new symmetry class of band insulator, not a variant of the integer quantum Hall effect, and it is the root of the three-dimensional case as well. Molenkamp's group then showed in HgTe quantum wells that the edge conductance is quantized at 2e^2/h and disappears as the sample is made wider, which is the quantitative signature the theory requires. The result has been reproduced by other groups and in other systems, and the interpretation has not changed in fifteen years. It is the clearest case on the list in which a simple general mechanism was identified, observed and understood, which is the standard I try to apply to every candidate including my own favourite, B005. I should also be honest that the original Kane-Mele graphene proposal is not itself the platform that was measured, because the spin-orbit gap of graphene is tiny; the concept came from Kane and Mele, the material came from elsewhere, and the citation has to say exactly that.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and the first round did not remove it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang identified HgTe as the material in which the effect should appear and gave the quantitative prediction of the critical thickness that Molenkamp's group then confirmed, Zhang is deceased, and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Roy and Hasan lies outside any three-name list. Kroll's point is fair: the experiment tested the BHZ model, and a citation worded as 'prediction then measurement' would be misleading. My answer is a citation that credits the concept and the observation separately, and does not say that Kane and Mele predicted the HgTe result. If the committee cannot accept this, B037 is the better choice. The 2016 prize and the sense in some quarters that topology is saturated also remain a risk, though I do not find them decisive on the science.

responses.point: Kroll says the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp citation leaves out the BHZ theory that the experiment actually tested, and that he would need a convincing answer before ranking B042 above the clock.
responses.response: I accept the factual point and have changed my wording because of it: the HgTe measurement was a test of the BHZ prediction, not of a statement by Kane and Mele about HgTe. What I would say in reply is that the prize can honour the discovery of the phase, that is, the Z2 invariant and the helical edge states, which is what Kane and Mele supplied and what makes the BHZ calculation meaningful in the first place. Molenkamp's measurement is then credited as the first observation of that phase, without attributing the material prediction to the theorists. The remaining gap, Zhang's death and the three-name cap, is a loss I cannot argue away. I do not expect this to move you above the clock, and I will not insist; but I think the question is whether the citation is accurate, not whether it is complete, and an accurate two-sided citation is possible.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B037 first, says she is relying on memory for the magic-wavelength priority history, and is careful about her own familiarity with the field.
responses.response: I appreciate the caution, and I would ask the same of myself for B042. As a theorist outside atomic physics I cannot judge the priority of the magic-wavelength proposal; that is for you, Johansson and Kroll, from the primary papers. If it holds up as you recall it, Katori for the concept and first demonstration and Ye for the accuracy and many-body frontier, then I think B037 has the cleaner attribution of the two candidates, and I have said I would not block it. What I would still ask is whether the part that is new relative to the 2005 comb and 2012 prizes can be stated as a physical statement (many neutral atoms interrogated without a lattice light shift) and not as an improvement of a figure of merit. I am not convinced that this is resolved.

responses.point: Olsson regrets losing Xue's quantum anomalous Hall experiment as a separate experimental discovery, and argues that omitting Mele would leave an arbitrary gap in the theory half.
responses.response: I agree that dropping Mele would be wrong: the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect are a joint result of Kane and Mele, and I cannot see an honest framing that credits one without the other. On Xue, I still think the quantum anomalous Hall effect belongs to a different story. It needs magnetic doping and broken time-reversal symmetry, and it is closer to the Haldane-Chern lineage that 2016 already touched. Folding it into the same prize would put the weakest part of the 2016 overlap argument into our citation. I would keep the citation narrow and let Xue's work be judged separately in a later year.

responses.point: Johansson moved to B037 and records that some colleagues find topology saturated, while accepting that Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is a defensible trio.
responses.response: I take the saturation worry seriously, and it is the argument against B042 that I find hardest to dismiss, because it is about the committee's overall taste and not about the science. The scientific answer is the symmetry-class distinction above: time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators are not contained in the 2016 citation. Whether that suffices is a judgement. I also note your point that the magic-wavelength idea is the part that makes the lattice clock new; if the atomic-physics members state that clearly and the primary papers confirm the priority, I would regard B037 as at least equally defensible, and I would vote for it before any other candidate than B042.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B006 as the experimental half of a mature discovery but says the three-name leadership credit is a compromise and that B037 would be better if it cannot be defended.
responses.response: I share your view that maturity and a clear experimental fact matter more than elegance, and I accept your earlier objection to B005, whose exponents are only partly tested; I no longer expect to defend it. On B006, I cannot judge the leadership history at the time of discovery, but I agree with Olsson and Pearce that leadership as such is a weak ground in the statute. Your own fallback to B037 therefore seems to me the right one, and it means that the committee has two candidates, B042 and B037, whose supporters each accept the other.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, prefers B037 for its two-name attribution and independent confirmation, while acknowledging that ion clocks reach comparable uncertainty and that he cannot settle the atomic-physics merit.
responses.response: I agree with the criteria you apply, independent confirmation and calibrated systematics, and B042 passes them: HgTe, InAs/GaSb and ARPES in Bi-based compounds. On ordering, I would rank B037 and B042 close to each other; I put B042 first because the new element is a symmetry-protected invariant and not a refinement of a device, and I would put B037 first if the atomic-physics members find the overlap with ion clocks and the frequency comb to be less of a problem than I do. What would change my ordering is a clear statement from them, based on the primary papers, that the Paris and Boulder groups do not have a priority claim that two names would misrepresent.

uncertainties: Whether an accurate two-sided citation (concept by Kane and Mele, first observation by Molenkamp) is acceptable when Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that the experiment tested and Zhang is deceased.
Whether the 2016 topological prize makes the committee unwilling to return to topology, whatever the symmetry-class distinction.
Whether the magic-wavelength priority and the overlap of B037 with the 2005 and 2012 prizes survive a check against primary papers, which I cannot do as a theorist outside atomic physics.
I am a theorist in statistical physics, not in topological band theory, and my assessment of B042 relies on the published record and on the colleagues' statements, not on first-hand expertise.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name from my profile. I am in the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), with no specific collaboration found; this does not require recusal. I have no tie to the groups behind B042 or B037.
